name: MonarchThreadPanel
title: ThreadPanel
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column with MonarchVirtualMessageList (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn) for the replies, MonarchChip to follow the thread and MonarchDivider; placed by the app in an MonarchBottomSheet or a supporting pane
summary: The panel of one conversation thread: the message it answers, a reply count divider, the replies pinned to the newest one, a follow chip, and the app's reply box pinned to the bottom.
whenToUse: When someone opens the replies to one message of a chat or channel: in a sheet on a phone, or in a pane beside the conversation at expanded width.
whenNotToUse: For the conversation itself, use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow. For discussions anchored to a document passage, use MonarchCommentThread or MonarchCommentsPanel.
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable fun <T> MonarchThreadPanel(replies: List<T>, key: (reply: T) -> Any, time: (reply: T) -> Long, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, replyCount: Int = replies.size, status: MonarchThreadPanelStatus = MonarchThreadPanelStatus.Ready, following: Boolean = false, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), authorId: (reply: T) -> String? = { null }, notice: String? = null, seenDelayMillis: Long = 400L, now: Long? = null, locale: Locale? = null, timeZone: String? = null, labels: MonarchThreadPanelLabels = MonarchThreadPanelLabels(), onClose: (() -> Unit)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onFollowingChange: (suspend (Boolean) -> Unit)? = null, onRepliesSeen: ((replyCount: Int) -> Unit)? = null, followIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, headerActions: (@Composable RowScope.() -> Unit)? = null, root: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, typing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, composer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, reply: @Composable LazyItemScope.(reply: T, context: MonarchVirtualMessageListContext<T>) -> Unit)
enum class MonarchThreadPanelStatus { Ready, Loading, Error, Deleted }

class MonarchThreadPanelLabels(title: String? = null, close: String? = null, follow: String? = null, following: String? = null, followedNotice: String? = null, unfollowedNotice: String? = null, followFailed: String? = null, replyCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, replies: String? = null, loading: String? = null, error: String? = null, deleted: String? = null, list: MonarchVirtualMessageListLabels? = null)

options.name: replies
options.description: The loaded replies, oldest first.

options.name: key
options.description: A stable, unique key per reply.

options.name: time
options.description: When a reply was sent, in epoch milliseconds (UTC), for day separators and grouping.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the panel. Give it a bounded height.

options.name: replyCount
options.description: The number of replies for the divider; can exceed the loaded replies.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready shows the replies; Loading placeholders; Error an error with Try again; Deleted a notice with Close.

options.name: following
options.description: The person follows the thread: the chip is selected and reads Following.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the replies; index 0 is the bottom row.

options.name: authorId
options.description: The author of a reply, for grouping consecutive replies.

options.name: notice
options.description: A note after the replies, such as Showing the first 500 replies.

options.name: seenDelayMillis
options.description: How long the replies stay on screen before onRepliesSeen.

options.name: now
options.description: The current time for Today and Yesterday; null reads the clock.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of the day separators; null uses the configuration's.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The time zone of the day separators. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, and optionally the list's.

options.name: onClose
options.description: Shows Close in the header and with a deleted thread.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again when the thread could not be loaded.

options.name: onFollowingChange
options.description: Follows or unfollows; shows the follow chip while Ready. Throw to announce a failure.

options.name: onRepliesSeen
options.description: Called with replyCount once the replies have been on screen for seenDelayMillis, and again when the count changes: mark the thread read here.

options.name: followIcon
options.description: The icon of the follow chip.

options.name: headerActions
options.description: Further header controls, before Close.

options.name: root
options.description: The message the thread answers, usually a MonarchMessageRow.

options.name: typing
options.description: Above the reply box, such as a MonarchTypingIndicator.

options.name: composer
options.description: The reply box, usually a MonarchMessageComposer, pinned under the replies.

options.name: reply
options.description: Draws one reply, usually a MonarchMessageRow with grouped = context.grouped.

states.name: ready
states.description: The root message, the reply count divider and the replies, newest at the bottom, with day separators.

states.name: following
states.description: The chip is selected and reads Following; changing it disables the chip until the app's function returns.

states.name: loading
states.description: A MonarchLoadingState with three rows, read once as Loading thread.

states.name: error
states.description: This thread couldn't be loaded, with Try again (MonarchInlineErrorRetry), or in the strong danger text role without onRetry.

states.name: deleted
states.description: This thread was deleted, announced, with Close.

appearance: No fill of its own, so it takes the sheet's or pane's surface. The heading uses the default text role, the reply count, the notice and the deleted text the muted text role, the dividers the subtle border role, and the follow chip the Material 3 filter chip roles Monarch maps from the theme. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's ThreadPanel takes the replies as children of a scrolling log; on Android they are items of a MonarchVirtualMessageList, so only the replies on screen are composed, day separators are added and consecutive replies group. The web's follow button with aria-pressed is a MonarchChip here. The web's close icon button is a Close text button because Monarch bundles no icons; a sheet also closes by swiping and with the back gesture. The web reports replies seen while the page is visible; on Android the delay runs while the panel is composed, and the app should not compose it while its screen is stopped. iOS has no entry for this id yet.
accessibility: The replies are a list named Replies; new replies are announced by MonarchVirtualMessageList.
The follow chip has the selected state and its text changes between Follow and Following; it is disabled while the change runs.
Following, unfollowing and a failure are announced through a polite live region that is always present.
The deleted notice is a polite live region.
Follow, Close and Try again have 48dp touch targets.
edgeCases: replyCount can be larger than the loaded replies; use notice to say how many are shown.
The root shows only once the replies reach the start of the thread, as the header of MonarchVirtualMessageList.
The follow chip is hidden while loading, after an error and for a deleted thread.
onRepliesSeen is called again when replyCount changes, after the delay.
The replies are a lazy list: give the panel a bounded height and do not put it in a vertically scrolling parent.
